subject: Seed hydration, staggered cutover, and rerank safety-net
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>, sre@acme.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Seed hydration proposal + staggered cutover windows (Acme)

Jordan / Acme SRE,

Thanks for the sync earlier — attaching a first-pass plan for seed hydration and a short rerank evaluation sample. Goal here is to stage a staggered backfill (wave A/B/C) to limit query impact and keep an immediate rollback path. High-level ask: please confirm acceptable cutover evenings (PST) and whether you can provide a 4-hour maintenance window for wave A.

Planned approach (summary):
- Snapshot current index (read-only) and export a delta list for seed IDs.
- Wave A: 10% priority documents (30M vectors) — run hydration + priming in staging then dry-run smoke queries.
- Wave B: 40% — larger batch with priming and rerank calibration.
- Wave C: remaining 50% after acceptance gates.
- Keep the old index and a hot fallback reranker for 72 hours post-cutover.

Preflight checklist attached: acme_seed_plan_v1.xlsx
Rerank sample (used for eval): rerank-eval-sample.jsonl

Questions for you:
1) Do the proposed evenings (Sept 9 / Sept 16 / Sept 23, 10pm-2am PST) look OK?
2) Can the SRE team enable a read-only replica for the snapshot step?
3) Any constraints on writing to the vector DB during priming (throttle limits)?

I suggest a short preflight call next Tue to lock windows and test small dry-run (10k vectors).

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: acme_seed_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), rerank-eval-sample.jsonl (jsonl sample)

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seed hydration proposal + staggered cutover windows (Acme)

Thanks Karthik — this looks sensible and conservative, which we appreciate. A few quick notes from the Acme side: 

- Evening windows: Sept 9 and Sept 16 are OK; Sept 23 is a hard no for us (end of quarter deploy freeze). Can we move wave C to Sept 30 if needed?
- Vector DB compatibility: we're on PolarisSearch v3.2 with read-replica support. Read-only replica is fine; we'll coordinate SRE to create one.
- Throttles: the DB enforces a soft write throttle at 200 writes/s per shard; we should avoid sustained higher throughput.

One more ask — will Redwood's priming process require altering vector schema or rolling index mapping changes? We want to avoid reindexing if possible.

Jordan
Director, Search & Relevance
Acme Analytics

Jordan / team — quick alignment from CSM/QA perspective. A couple of operational concerns and acceptance gates to call out so the implementation windows are useful to QA: 

Acceptance gates (must pass before promoting wave to next):
- Smoke query set: 150 queries from rerank-eval-sample.jsonl (diverse intents) — precision@10 improvement within +/- 2% of baseline or no statistically significant degradation.
- Latency gate: p95 must remain within 1.25x of current p95 for 24 hours after each wave.
- Error gate: no >1% error-rate spike for top traffic routes.

Operational asks:
- We need one Redwood engineer on-call during the 4-hour window for immediate rollback.
- Please confirm whether Acme can keep the read-rep for at least 96 hours (we prefer 72 but will accept 96 for safety).

If those gates look ok, we'll run a 10k dry-run on Sept 4 (non-production staging) to exercise the pipeline and verify the smoke queries.

-naomi
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Seed hydration proposal + staggered cutover windows (Acme)

Couple technical clarifications from the implementation lead side: 

- No schema changes required on PolarisSearch for priming — we will write vectors into the existing index with the same dimensionality. Good call to avoid reindexing.
- Backfill throughput: target 180 writes/s/shard to stay under your soft throttle, with an adaptive throttle controller that backs off when we see increased latency.
- Batching: we'll use 512-vector batches for GPU efficiency during hydration; that should map to ~2.5MB payloads per batch depending on vector type.
- KV cache warmup: we will run a priming pass that kicks the top-100 queries through the new index immediately after each wave to populate caches. This is time-boxed to 15 minutes per wave.
- Fallback plan: if p95 latency exceeds gate or precision regresses significantly, we'll flip traffic back to the snapshot index (DNS-based routing) and run a rollback sweep to restore baseline. Keep the old index accessible for 72 hours.

I'll be on-call for wave A and will coordinate with Redwood infra to monitor token throughput.

-Marissa
Engineering Lead, Implementation
Redwood Inference
